## How We Analyzed 312 Programmes {background-color="#f8f9fa"}

```{=html}
<div style="text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0.8em;">
<h3 style="color: #1e3a5f; margin: 0; font-size: 1.1em;">Traditional approach would take months...</h3>
</div>

<div style="display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; gap: 1.5em;">

<!-- Manual approach -->
<div style="text-align: center; padding: 1em 2em; background: #ffebee; border-radius: 12px; width: 380px;">
<div style="font-size: 1em; font-weight: bold; color: #c62828; margin-bottom: 0.3em;">Manual Coding</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.85em; color: #555;">
• Read each document <br>• Code conditions by hand<br>
<strong>~2 hours × 312 docs = 624+ researcher hours</strong>
</div>
</div>

<div style="font-size: 2em; color: #1e3a5f;">→</div>

<!-- LLM approach -->
<div style="text-align: center; padding: 1em 2em; background: #e8f5e9; border-radius: 12px; width: 380px;">
<div style="font-size: 1em; font-weight: bold; color: #388e3c; margin-bottom: 0.3em;">LLM Extraction</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.85em; color: #555;">
• Structured prompts <br>• Consistent coding<br>
<strong>~2 minutes × 312 docs = 10 hours total</strong>
</div>
</div>

</div>
```

::: {.fragment style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.8em; padding: 0.6em; background: #e3f2fd; border-radius: 10px;"}
**60x faster** while maintaining analytical rigor
:::

::: {.notes}
- LLMs allow us to analyze at scale what would be impossible manually
- Key innovation: structured extraction with validation
:::

## Four Definitions of Success

```{=html}
<div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 1em; margin-top: 0.5em;">

<div style="background: linear-gradient(135deg, #a8b5e6 0%, #b8a4c9 100%); color: #333; padding: .5em; border-radius: 12px;">
<div style="font-size: 2em; font-weight: bold;">16%</div>
<div style="font-size: 1.1em; font-weight: bold;">High Performance</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.85em; opacity: 0.9;">Overall A++/A+/A scores <br>— <em>The "gold standard"</em></div>
</div>

<div style="background: linear-gradient(135deg, #a8e6cf 0%, #88d8b0 100%); color: #333; padding: .5em; border-radius: 12px;">
<div style="font-size: 2em; font-weight: bold;">80%</div>
<div style="font-size: 1.1em; font-weight: bold;">Impact Achievement</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.85em; opacity: 0.9;">Achieved intended results <br>— <em>Did what it set out to do</em></div>
</div>

<div style="background: linear-gradient(135deg, #ffc3d0 0%, #ffb3ba 100%); color: #333; padding: .5em; border-radius: 12px;">
<div style="font-size: 2em; font-weight: bold;">69%</div>
<div style="font-size: 1.1em; font-weight: bold;">Sustainability</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.85em; opacity: 0.9;">Results will last <br>— <em>Beyond the programme</em></div>
</div>

<div style="background: linear-gradient(135deg, #ffe5b4 0%, #ffd699 100%); color: #333; padding: .5em; border-radius: 12px;">
<div style="font-size: 2em; font-weight: bold;">34%</div>
<div style="font-size: 1.1em; font-weight: bold;">Equity Outcomes</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.85em; opacity: 0.9;">Reached marginalized groups <br>— <em>The hardest to achieve</em></div>
</div>

</div>
```

::: {.notes}
- High Performance is rare (16%) — the elite tier.
- Impact is common (80%) — most programmes deliver.
- Sustainability is harder (69%) — lasting change is tough.
- Equity is hardest (34%) — inclusion requires intention.
:::

## How We Extracted: Example 1 {background-color="#f8f9fa"}

```{=html}
<div style="margin-top: 0.3em;">

<div style="font-size: 0.75em; font-weight: bold; color: #1e3a5f; margin-bottom: 0.4em;">Strategic Clarity (IFFIm Programme)</div>

<div style="display: flex; gap: 0.8em;">

<div style="flex: 1; background: #1e3a5f; color: #a8e6cf; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; font-family: monospace; font-size: 0.5em; line-height: 1.4;">
<span style="color: #ffc3d0; font-weight: bold;">PROMPT:</span><br>
Definition: Clarity of programme purpose,<br>
presence of Theory of Change, explicit<br>
indicators and linked outputs.<br><br>
Look for: ToC diagram, logical framework,<br>
indicator matrix, output-outcome chains<br><br>
<span style="color: #fff8e1;">Score:</span><br>
&nbsp;1.00 = ToC fully detailed with indicators<br>
&nbsp;0.67 = ToC present, some indicators<br>
&nbsp;0.33 = Vague logic mentioned<br>
&nbsp;0.00 = No ToC/indicators
</div>

<div style="flex: 1.3; background: #f5f5f5; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.5em; line-height: 1.4;">
<span style="font-weight: bold; color: #388e3c;">REAL OUTPUT:</span><br><br>
<span style="color: #1976d2; font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.1em;">"score": 0.67</span><br><br>
<span style="font-weight: bold;">"evidence":</span> <em>"Key performance measures in the 2021-25 strategic period are to: Vaccinate 300 million children; Save 7-8 million lives; Reduce the number of children who have never received a vaccine by 25%"</em><br><br>
<span style="font-weight: bold;">"justification":</span> "Clear outcome-level indicators provided, but no detailed Theory of Change or output-outcome chains explicitly documented."
</div>

</div>

<div style="margin-top: 0.5em; background: #e8f5e9; padding: 0.4em; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 0.55em; text-align: center;">
<strong>Key:</strong> LLM provides score + evidence quote + justification → enables human audit
</div>

</div>
```

::: {.notes}
- This is a real extraction from the IFFIm programme.
- Score of 0.67 means "more in than out" — indicators exist but no detailed ToC.
:::

## How We Extracted: Example 2 {background-color="#f8f9fa"}

```{=html}
<div style="margin-top: 0.3em;">

<div style="font-size: 0.75em; font-weight: bold; color: #1e3a5f; margin-bottom: 0.4em;">Shared Governance (PSIG Programme)</div>

<div style="display: flex; gap: 0.8em;">

<div style="flex: 1; background: #1e3a5f; color: #a8e6cf; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; font-family: monospace; font-size: 0.5em; line-height: 1.4;">
<span style="color: #ffc3d0; font-weight: bold;">PROMPT:</span><br>
Definition: Extent of partner decision power
in governance: steering committee seats,
co-chairs, partner voting rights, formal ToR.<br><br>
Look for: Governance structure, steering
committee composition, partner roles<br><br>
<span style="color: #fff8e1;">Score:</span><br>
&nbsp;1.00 = Partners have formal voting/co-chair<br>
&nbsp;0.67 = Partners on committees, no voting<br>
&nbsp;0.33 = Consultation only<br>
&nbsp;0.00 = FCDO-led only
</div>

<div style="flex: 1.3; background: #f5f5f5; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 0.5em; line-height: 1.4;">
<span style="font-weight: bold; color: #388e3c;">REAL OUTPUT:</span><br><br>
<span style="color: #1976d2; font-weight: bold; font-size: 1.1em;">"score": 0.67</span><br><br>
<span style="font-weight: bold;">"evidence":</span> <em>"An Investment Committee which reviews and approves investments, with members mutually agreed, will be established"</em><br><br>
<span style="font-weight: bold;">"justification":</span> "SIDBI/SVCL have decision-making authority via the Investment Committee (joint DFID-SIDBI members), but no formal voting rights for local partners or beneficiaries are mentioned."
</div>

</div>

<div style="margin-top: 0.5em; background: #fff3e0; padding: 0.4em; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 0.55em; text-align: center;">
<strong>Same logic applied to all 14 conditions × 312 programmes = 4,368 scored extractions</strong>
</div>

</div>
```

::: {.notes}
- Second example: Shared Governance from the Poorest States Inclusive Growth Programme.
- Score of 0.67 = partners have some decision power but not formal voting rights.
- Shows how different conditions use the same structured approach.
:::

## The Scoring Rubric {background-color="#f8f9fa"}

```{=html}
<div style="margin-top: 0.3em;">

<div style="font-size: 0.75em; font-weight: bold; color: #1e3a5f; margin-bottom: 0.4em;">Fuzzy-set calibration (0 to 1):</div>

<table style="width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 0.65em;">
<thead>
<tr style="background: #1e3a5f; color: white;">
<th style="padding: 0.4em; text-align: center; width: 12%;">Score</th>
<th style="padding: 0.4em; text-align: left;">Business Case (Design Intent)</th>
<th style="padding: 0.4em; text-align: left;">Annual Review (Implementation Reality)</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr style="background: #e8f5e9;">
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; color: #388e3c; font-size: 1.1em;">1.00</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Fully embedded in design (ToC/contract/budgeted)</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Demonstrated with evidence and indicators</td>
</tr>
<tr style="background: #fff8e1;">
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; color: #f57c00; font-size: 1.1em;">0.67</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Clearly stated commitment, limited operational detail</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Partially implemented or documented steps taken</td>
</tr>
<tr style="background: #fff3e0;">
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; color: #e65100; font-size: 1.1em;">0.33</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Mentioned as aspiration without concrete mechanism</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Discussed or recommended to be improved</td>
</tr>
<tr style="background: #ffebee;">
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; color: #c62828; font-size: 1.1em;">0.00</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Not present in Business Case</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">No evidence in Annual Review</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<div style="display: flex; gap: 0.8em; margin-top: 0.6em;">

<div style="flex: 1; background: #e3f2fd; padding: 0.5em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #1976d2;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.65em; color: #1976d2;">Binary Threshold</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #555;">Score ≥ 0.67 → Condition <strong>present</strong> (1)<br>Score < 0.67 → Condition <strong>absent</strong> (0)</div>
</div>

<div style="flex: 1; background: #f3e5f5; padding: 0.5em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #7b1fa2;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.65em; color: #7b1fa2;">Outcome Scoring</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #555;">Performance: A++=1.0, A+=0.8, A=0.6...<br>Other outcomes: Same 4-point scale</div>
</div>

</div>

</div>
```

::: {.notes}
- Fuzzy-set scores give us more nuance than binary.
- Binary threshold at 0.67 = "more in than out" of the set.
- Anchored descriptions ensure consistent scoring across documents.
:::

## The Traditional Question {background-color="#f8f9fa"}

::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 2em; margin-top: .5em;"}
"Which **factors** predict success?"
:::

::: {style="text-align: center; color: #666; margin-top: .5em;"}
*Regression logic: each factor in isolation*
:::

::: {.fragment style="margin-top: 2em; padding: 1em; background: #fff3cd; border-radius: 8px; text-align: center;"}
**Problem:** Assumes factors work independently — but in reality, success depends on *combinations*
:::

## The Configurational Question {background-color="#1e3a5f"}

::: {style="color: white;"}

::: {style="text-align: center; font-size: 2em; margin-top: .5em;"}
"What **combinations** of factors lead to success?"
:::

::: {style="text-align: center; opacity: 0.9; margin-top: 1em;"}
*QCA logic: configurations, not individual effects*
:::

::: {.fragment style="margin-top: 2em; padding: 1em; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.15); border-radius: 8px; text-align: center;"}
**Key insight:** Multiple pathways can lead to the same outcome (equifinality)
:::

:::

::: {.notes}
- Traditional evaluation asks "What predicts success?" — each factor in isolation.
- We ask "What combinations of factors reliably lead to success?" — that's configurationalism.
:::

## Think of it like baking {background-color="#f8f9fa"}

```{=html}
<style>
/* Row and card layout */
.cards-row {
  display: flex;
  gap: 1em;
  margin-top: 1em;

  box-sizing: border-box;
}

/* Card base style */
.card {
  flex: 1;
  padding: .5em;
  border-radius: 2px;
  text-align: center;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;

  height: auto;          /* avoid hardcoded unequal heights */
  min-height: 260px;     /* optional minimum so small screens still look good */
}

/* content styling */
.card .emoji { font-size: 1em; line-height: 1; }

/* colors */
.card.yellow { background: #fff3cd; }
.card.green  { background: #d4edda; }
</style>

<div class="cards-row">

  <!-- whole card is a fragment: first click reveals the left card -->
  <div class="card yellow fragment" role="group" aria-label="Necessary">
    <div class="emoji">🥚</div>
    <div class="title">Necessary</div>
    <div class="text">Eggs are required<br> for cake.<br>But eggs alone ≠ cake.</div>
  </div>

  <!-- second click reveals the right card -->
  <div class="card green fragment" role="group" aria-label="Sufficient">
    <div class="emoji">📋</div>
    <div class="title">Sufficient</div>

  </div>

</div>
```

::: {.fragment style="text-align: center; margin-top: 1.5em; font-size: 1.2em;"}
**QCA finds the recipes, not just the ingredients.**
:::

::: {.notes}
- Use the baking analogy for non-technical audiences.
- Necessary = you can't skip it. Sufficient = it works reliably.
:::

```{=html}
<div style="text-align: center; margin-bottom: 0.3em;">

</div>

<div style="display: flex; justify-content: center; gap: 1.5em; align-items: flex-start;">

<!-- Necessary Venn: Success is SUBSET of Condition -->
<div style="text-align: center;">
<svg width="240" height="180" viewBox="0 0 240 180">
  <!-- Outer circle: Condition -->
  <circle cx="120" cy="90" r="80" fill="#bbdefb" stroke="#1976d2" stroke-width="3"/>

</svg>
<div style="font-size: 1em; font-weight: bold; color: #1976d2;">NECESSARY</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #777;"><em>"Can't succeed without it"</em></div>
</div>

<!-- Sufficient Venn: Condition is SUBSET of Success -->
<div style="text-align: center;">
<svg width="240" height="180" viewBox="0 0 240 180">
  <!-- Outer circle: Success -->
  <circle cx="120" cy="90" r="80" fill="#c8e6c9" stroke="#388e3c" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Inner circle: Condition (inside success) -->
  <circle cx="120" cy="105" r="42" fill="#388e3c"/>
  <!-- Labels -->
  <text x="120" y="35" text-anchor="middle" fill="#388e3c" font-weight="bold" font-size="12">Success</text>
  <text x="120" y="110" text-anchor="middle" fill="white" font-weight="bold" font-size="12">Condition</text>
</svg>
<div style="font-size: 1em; font-weight: bold; color: #388e3c;">SUFFICIENT</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #777;"><em>"If present, always succeeds"</em></div>
</div>

<!-- Both: Overlapping Venn -->
<div style="text-align: center;">
<svg width="240" height="180" viewBox="0 0 240 180">
  <!-- Circle A: Condition -->
  <circle cx="85" cy="90" r="65" fill="#bbdefb" fill-opacity="0.7" stroke="#1976d2" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Circle B: Success -->
  <circle cx="155" cy="90" r="65" fill="#c8e6c9" fill-opacity="0.7" stroke="#388e3c" stroke-width="3"/>
  <!-- Labels -->
  <text x="45" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#1976d2" font-weight="bold" font-size="11">Condition</text>
  <text x="195" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#388e3c" font-weight="bold" font-size="11">Success</text>
  <text x="120" y="95" text-anchor="middle" fill="#333" font-weight="bold" font-size="11">Both</text>
</svg>
<div style="font-size: 1em; font-weight: bold; color: #f57c00;">QCA FINDS</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.7em; color: #777;"><em>Both types</em></div>
</div>

</div>
```

::: {.fragment style="text-align: center; margin-top: 0.3em; padding: 0.5em; background: #fff3e0; border-radius: 10px; border-left: 4px solid #f57c00; font-size: 0.9em;"}
**QCA finds both:** *necessary* (must-haves) AND *sufficient* (guarantees success)
:::


## Understanding QCA Metrics {background-color="#f0f4f8"}

```{=html}
<div style="display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 0.8em; margin-top: 0.3em;">

<div style="background: #e8f5e9; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #388e3c;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #388e3c; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">🎯 Necessity Consistency</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #333; line-height: 1.4;">
<strong>Question:</strong> When outcome is present, is the condition also present?
<br><strong>Threshold:</strong> ≥0.90 (condition in 90%+ of successful cases)
<br><em style="color: #666;">High = condition is a "must-have"</em>
</div>
</div>

<div style="background: #e3f2fd; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #1976d2;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #1976d2; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">📏 Sufficiency Consistency (incl.cut)</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #333; line-height: 1.4;">
<strong>Question:</strong> When condition pattern is present, does outcome follow?
<br><strong>Our threshold:</strong> incl.cut = 0.85 (85% of cases succeed)
<br><em style="color: #666;">High = pathway reliably produces success</em>
</div>
</div>

<div style="background: #fce4ec; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #c2185b;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #c2185b; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">📊 Coverage</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #333; line-height: 1.4;">
<strong>Question:</strong> What % of successful cases does this pathway explain?
<br><strong>Our solutions:</strong> 65-75% coverage (3 valid outcomes)
<br><em style="color: #666;">High = pathways capture most routes to success</em>
</div>
</div>

<div style="background: #fff3e0; padding: 0.6em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #f57c00;">
<div style="font-weight: bold; color: #f57c00; font-size: 0.8em; margin-bottom: 0.2em;">🔢 Frequency Threshold</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #333; line-height: 1.4;">
<strong>Question:</strong> Minimum cases to consider a pathway empirically grounded?
<br><strong>Our thresholds:</strong> 2 (rare outcomes) or 3 (common outcomes)
<br><em style="color: #666;">Balances pattern detection with empirical support</em>
</div>
</div>

</div>
```

::: {.fragment style="margin-top: 0.3em; padding: 0.4em; background: #f5f5f5; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 0.6em; text-align: center;"}
**Key thresholds:** Necessity ≥0.90 | Sufficiency (incl.cut) ≥0.85 | n.cut = 2-3 depending on outcome prevalence
:::

## Methodology: Adaptive Thresholds {background-color="#f0f4f8"}

```{=html}
<div style="margin-top: 0.3em;">
<div style="font-size: 0.75em; font-weight: bold; color: #1e3a5f; margin-bottom: 0.4em;">Why adaptive n.cut thresholds?</div>

<div style="font-size: 0.6em; color: #333; margin-bottom: 0.5em;">
With 14 conditions (2^14 = 16,384 configurations), finding meaningful pathways requires balancing specificity with empirical support. We use outcome-specific n.cut thresholds based on outcome prevalence.
</div>

<table style="width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; font-size: 0.55em;">
<thead>
<tr style="background: #1e3a5f; color: white;">
<th style="padding: 0.4em;">Outcome</th>
<th style="padding: 0.4em;">Prevalence</th>
<th style="padding: 0.4em;">n.cut</th>
<th style="padding: 0.4em;">Rationale</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr style="background: #e8eaf6;">
<td style="padding: 0.35em;"><strong>HIGH_PERFORMANCE</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center;">15.7%</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; color: #5c6bc0;">2</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Rare outcome, lower threshold needed</td>
</tr>
<tr style="background: #e8f5e9;">
<td style="padding: 0.35em;"><strong>IMPACT</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center;">79.5%</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; color: #388e3c;">3</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Common outcome, standard threshold</td>
</tr>
<tr style="background: #fce4ec;">
<td style="padding: 0.35em;"><strong>SUSTAINABILITY</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center;">69.2%</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; color: #c2185b;">3</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Common outcome, standard threshold</td>
</tr>
<tr style="background: #fff8e1;">
<td style="padding: 0.35em;"><strong>EQUITY_OUTCOMES</strong></td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center;">33.7%</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em; text-align: center; font-weight: bold; color: #f57c00;">2</td>
<td style="padding: 0.35em;">Less common, lower threshold</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

<div style="margin-top: 0.4em; font-size: 0.55em; color: #666;">
<strong>incl.cut = 0.85</strong> for all outcomes (consistency threshold) | <strong>Parsimonious solutions</strong> reported
</div>
</div>
```

## Outcome 1: High Performance {background-color="#a8b5e6"}

```{=html}
<div style="display: flex; gap: 1em; margin-top: 0.2em;">

<div style="flex: 0.8; text-align: center;">
<div style="font-size: 1.8em; font-weight: bold; color: #1e3a5f;">16%</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.6em; color: #333;">49 programmes</div>
<div style="font-size: 0.55em; color: #c62828; margin-top: 0.3em;"><strong>No consistent<br>pathways</strong></div>
</div>

<div style="flex: 2.5;">
<div style="background: white; padding: 0.4em; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.1);">

<div style="font-size: 0.6em; font-weight: bold; color: #5c6bc0; margin-bottom: 0.3em;">Necessity-Dominated Outcome</div>

<div style="font-size: 0.5em; color: #333; line-height: 1.5; padding: 0.5em;">
<p><strong>Finding:</strong> The QCA sufficiency analysis did not produce pathways meeting the 0.85 consistency threshold.</p>

<p><strong>What this means:</strong></p>
<ul style="margin: 0.3em 0; padding-left: 1.2em;">
<li>High Performance is <em>necessity-dominated</em> — success requires many conditions</li>
<li>No simple "recipe" exists — requires most necessary conditions simultaneously</li>
<li>Solution consistency: ~63% (below 85% threshold)</li>
<li>Solution coverage: ~99% (almost all cases covered, but inconsistently)</li>
</ul>
</div>

<div style="font-size: 0.45em; margin-top: 0.3em; padding: 0.3em; background: #fff3e0; border-radius: 4px;">
<strong>Interpretation:</strong> Best predicted by presence of ALL necessary conditions (ImpactStrategy, StrategicAgendaClarity, SharedGovernance, OutputsAccessible, PartnershipEquity)
</div>

</div>
</div>

</div>
```

::: {.fragment style="margin-top: 0.3em; padding: 0.4em; background: #ffebee; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 0.6em; text-align: center;"}
**HIGH_PERFORMANCE is necessity-dominated**: 5 necessary conditions (consistency >0.90) must be present. No single pathway reliably guarantees success.
:::

## Key Messages for Policy Makers {background-color="#1e3a5f"}

::: {style="color: white;"}

```{=html}
<div style="display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.5em; margin-top: 0.3em;">

<div class="fragment" style="background: rgba(168,230,207,0.2); padding: 0.5em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #a8e6cf; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6em;">
<div style="font-size: 1.3em; width: 35px; text-align: center;">📦</div>
<div>
<div style="font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em;">"Accessibility is the gateway to impact"</div>
<div style="opacity: 0.9; font-size: 0.6em;">OutputsAccessible <em>alone</em> is sufficient for impact. Prioritize open access, plain-language outputs, stakeholder-friendly formats.</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="fragment" style="background: rgba(255,229,180,0.2); padding: 0.5em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #ffe5b4; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6em;">
<div style="font-size: 1.3em; width: 35px; text-align: center;">♀️</div>
<div>
<div style="font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em;">"GESI is non-negotiable for equity"</div>
<div style="opacity: 0.9; font-size: 0.6em;">Gender & Social Inclusion appears in 100% of equity pathways. Embed from design — not an afterthought.</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="fragment" style="background: rgba(255,195,208,0.2); padding: 0.5em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #ffc3d0; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6em;">
<div style="font-size: 1.3em; width: 35px; text-align: center;">🔀</div>
<div>
<div style="font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em;">"Pick your sustainability strategy"</div>
<div style="opacity: 0.9; font-size: 0.6em;">Two paths: Dual outputs (Accessible + Capacity) OR Ownership (Governance + Embedding + Long-term funding). Choose deliberately.</div>
</div>
</div>

<div class="fragment" style="background: rgba(168,181,230,0.2); padding: 0.5em; border-radius: 8px; border-left: 4px solid #a8b5e6; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.6em;">
<div style="font-size: 1.3em; width: 35px; text-align: center;">⚖️</div>
<div>
<div style="font-weight: bold; font-size: 0.85em;">"You can't optimize for everything"</div>
<div style="opacity: 0.9; font-size: 0.6em;">HIGH_PERFORMANCE fails completely. Be explicit about which outcomes matter most. Stop pretending every programme can maximize all.</div>
</div>
</div>

</div>
```

:::

::: {.notes}
**MESSAGE 1: "Accessibility is the gateway to impact"**

What it means: When we looked at which programmes achieved their intended IMPACT, we found that making outputs accessible to beneficiaries was the SINGLE most powerful factor. In fact, it's SUFFICIENT on its own — meaning if a programme makes its outputs accessible, it reliably achieves impact, regardless of other factors.

What "accessible" means: Reports available in local languages, findings shared in formats stakeholders can use (not just academic papers), training materials people can actually access, policy briefs for decision-makers.

Why it matters: This is the simplest lever. You don't need complex governance or 10-year funding. Just make sure what you produce actually reaches people who can use it.

---

**MESSAGE 2: "GESI is non-negotiable for equity"**

What GESI means: Gender Equality and Social Inclusion — deliberately designing programmes to reach women, girls, disabled people, ethnic minorities, the poorest, and other marginalized groups.

What the finding shows: EVERY SINGLE pathway that led to equity outcomes included GESI. 100%. With 0.987 consistency (near-perfect reliability). This means you CANNOT achieve equity outcomes without intentionally building GESI into your programme design.

Why it matters: This settles debates about whether GESI is "nice to have" vs essential. For equity outcomes, it's essential. Period. It must be in the Theory of Change from day one, not added as a checkbox later.

---

**MESSAGE 3: "Pick your sustainability strategy"**

What it means: We found TWO genuinely different ways to achieve sustainability:

PATH A - "Outputs strategy": Make outputs BOTH accessible AND build capacity to use them. Example: A health programme that produces treatment guidelines (accessible) AND trains local health workers to apply them (capacity).

PATH B - "Ownership strategy": Combine shared governance with local embedding and long-term funding. Example: A governance programme where local partners co-manage decisions, activities are integrated into local government systems, and funding is committed for 5+ years.

Why it matters: These require DIFFERENT investments. Don't assume you can do both with the same design. Choose which path fits your context and resource accordingly.

---

**MESSAGE 4: "You can't optimize for everything"**

What it means: We tried to find configurations that lead to programmes scoring A++ or A+ on ALL dimensions (our HIGH_PERFORMANCE outcome). The QCA FAILED — no reliable pathway exists. The consistency was only 0.286 (way below the 0.85 threshold needed).

Why this happens: Different outcomes may require different — even conflicting — design choices. One impact pathway actually includes the ABSENCE of GESI, suggesting a potential tension between "quick impact" and "equitable impact."

Why it matters: Stop pretending every programme can maximize impact AND sustainability AND equity AND cost-effectiveness simultaneously. Be honest about priorities. If equity matters most, accept that some "efficient" impact paths are off-limits.
:::

::: {.notes}
- Four actionable recommendations.
- Foundations = protect. Pathways = allow choice. Expectations = be humble. Equity = invest heavily.
:::
